stresses: A COMPOUND, SINGLE-SENTENCE BLANKET DISCLAIMER covering FOUR distinct topics at once ('no heating checked, no attic, no blower door, no safety tests') -- exercises rule 4's requirement to write ONE disclaimer per named thing (hvac group, attic group, blowerDoor named set, healthTests named set) rather than one disclaimer whose topic lists everything but whose scope only covers one; this is the ANNOTATOR_GUIDE.md's own cited example transcript for that rule. Only ONE component was actually inspected (the DHW unit), stated with a fused fuel+type mention ('electric tank') and a location ('in the garage'), with no retractions and no genuinely contested enum mapping. A trailing 'nothing else today' needs no disclaimer of its own (rule 4.4 -- topic-free). A vague qualitative age impression ('looked pretty new') that must NOT be inferred into a dhwAge band -- the guide's own 'model year from the plate looked worn' inference trap, applied to a condition gesture instead. A secondhand, auditor-unverified comfort complaint (the wife's cold-upstairs remark) has no matching leaf anywhere in the 51 (SCHEMA FINDING -- comfort complaints; see RECONCILIATION.md) and is explicitly disclaimed by the auditor as 'not a measurement' -- exercises rule 3's second-speaker-attribution guard and rule 9's no-write-target guard simultaneously.

The trailing 'nothing else today' names nothing specific, per rule 4's fourth bullet, so it gets no disclaimer of its own. Wall and window groups are never mentioned at all in this transcript (not even as part of the compound disclaimer sentence, which names 'attic' and 'blower door' individually but not 'wall', 'window', or 'shell'/'envelope') and are left at their default unmentioned rather than swept into a 'shell' namedSet the auditor never actually invoked.
